extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent owners, and patent practitioners involved in ex parte reexamination proceedings before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards from the MPEP governing responses, extensions, service, entry of papers, and examiner handling in ex parte reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic 1-month extension for first response after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing of any timely first response to a final rejection will be construed as including a request to extend the shortened statutory period for an additional month; this automatic 1-month extension applies only to the first response after final and does not apply once the Notice of Appeal has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An advisory Office action (PTOL-467) should state the extension. The Office will notify the patent owner that an appeal brief is due two months from the notice of appeal if a Notice of Appeal has been filed; in that instance extensions are governed by 37 CFR 1.550(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner notification and timing after a timely response filed post-final
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner is entitled to know the examiner’s ruling on a timely response filed after final rejection before being required to file a notice of appeal; examiners will normally complete a response to an amendment after final rejection within 5 days after receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the advisory action cannot be mailed in sufficient time for the patent owner to consider and act before termination of prosecution, the examiner should grant additional time and set it forth in the advisory Office action (e.g., PTOL-467).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of response period by advisory action (integer months, max 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory action (PTOL-467) may extend the period for response by filling in an integer number of months (2-6) from the mailing date of the final rejection; fractional months should not be indicated and the period cannot exceed 6 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appropriate response (e.g., second amendment or notice of appeal) must be filed within the extended period. If a subsequent amendment is filed it must place the reexamination in condition for allowance or prosecution will be terminated under 37 CFR 1.550(d) unless an appeal was timely filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time to submit affidavits after final rejection (grant without prejudice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for extension of time after final rejection to submit an affidavit may be granted, but such grant is without prejudice to the examiner’s right to question necessity and timeliness of the affidavit; if the showing is insufficient the examiner may deny entry of the affidavit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant of extension merely keeps prosecution from terminating while allowing opportunity to present the affidavit or take other action. The affidavit must still meet requirements (37 CFR 1.113); admission or refusal to admit the affidavit does not operate to save prosecution from termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply requirements under 37 CFR 1.111
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office action after the first examination is adverse, the applicant or patent owner must reply and request reconsideration or further examination, with or without amendment; the reply must be reduced to writing which distinctly and specifically points out the supposed errors and must reply to every ground of objection and rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply must present arguments pointing out the specific distinctions believed to render the claims patentable over applied references. A general allegation that the claims define a patentable invention without specifics does not comply. Requests to hold form objections in abeyance may be made where appropriate. Replies must appear to be a bona fide attempt to advance the application or reexamination to final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental replies limitations (37 CFR 1.111(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental reply that is supplemental to a reply in compliance with 1.111(b) will not be entered as a matter of right except where clearly limited to: (A) cancellation of claim(s); (B) adoption of examiner suggestion(s); (C) placement in condition for allowance/notice of intent to issue reexamination certificate; (D) reply to Office requirement made after the first reply; (E) correction of informalities (typographical errors); or (F) simplification of issues for appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental reply filed during a period when action is suspended under § 1.103(a) or (c) will be entered. The examiner may enter a supplemental reply after a cursory review if it meets one or more of these conditions. Unentered supplemental replies will not be entered later when a response to a subsequent Office action is filed; their contents must be included in a proper subsequent response if they are to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment content requirements (point out patentable novelty)
rubrics_metrics.description: When amending in reply to a rejection, the applicant or patent owner must clearly point out the patentable novelty believed present in the claims in view of the art and must show how the amendments avoid such references or objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies in both applications and reexamination proceedings; arguments and amendments should specifically address the cited references and objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of ex parte reexamination (37 CFR 1.550): special dispatch and response periods
rubrics_metrics.description: All ex parte reexamination proceedings (including appeals) will be conducted with special dispatch. After issuance of the order and expiration for responses, examination will be conducted under §§ 1.104–1.116. Patent owner will be given at least 30 days to respond to any Office action; responses may include statements, proposed amendments, or new claims to place the patent in condition where all claims, if amended as proposed, would be patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner normally given 2 months to respond; extensions only under 37 CFR 1.550(c). 37 CFR 1.136 does not apply in reexamination proceedings. The certificate of mailing/transmission and Express Mail procedures may be used to file responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time in reexamination (sufficient cause, petition fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time for any action by a patent owner in an ex parte reexamination will be extended only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified; any request must be filed on or before the day action is due and must be accompanied by the petition fee in § 1.17(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mere filing of a request does not effect an extension. See § 1.304(a) for extensions for filing notices of appeal or commencing civil actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to file timely and appropriate response (termination and certificate)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner fails to file a timely and appropriate response to any Office action or any required interview statement, the ex parte reexamination proceeding will be terminated and the Director will proceed to issue a certificate under § 1.570 in accordance with the last Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delayed responses may be excused if shown to the Director to be unavoidable (petition under § 1.137(a)) or accepted if unintentional (petition under § 1.137(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirements in third-party requested reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing of a request for ex parte reexamination by a third party, any document filed by either the patent owner or the third party requester must be served on the other party in the manner provided by § 1.248 and must reflect service or it may be refused consideration by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submitting party must attach a certificate of service stating the name and address of the party served and the method of service; a copy of the certificate of service must be attached to the copy served. Papers lacking required proof of service may be denied consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active participation of third-party requester ends with reply (1.535)
rubrics_metrics.description: The active participation of the ex parte reexamination requester ends with the reply pursuant to § 1.535; no further submissions on behalf of the requester will be acknowledged or considered unless in accordance with § 1.510 or § 1.535, or entered prior to the order under § 1.525.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions by third parties after the order must meet § 1.501(a) and will be treated accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on filing third-party papers by patent owner (37 CFR 1.550(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner must not file papers on behalf of a third party; if a third party paper accompanies or is submitted as part of a timely filed response, the response and the third party paper are improper and the entire submission will be returned, and the third party paper will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision returning the improper submission should provide an appropriate extension under 37 CFR 1.550(c) to refile the patent owner response without the third party paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission not fully responsive to a non-final Office action (definition and examiner options)
rubrics_metrics.description: A response is 'not fully responsive' when: (A) a bona fide response is filed before expiration; (B) before expiration of the permissible response period; and (C) through apparent oversight or inadvertence some point necessary to a full response has been omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If (A)-(C) met, prosecution should not be terminated. Examiner may: (A) waive deficiencies if not serious and act on submission; (B) accept amendment as response but issue new Office action identifying omission and new time period; or (C) notify patent owner that the response must be completed within the remaining response period (or extension) to avoid termination. For minor deficiencies the examiner may simply act and issue new action reiterating unaddressed items. For serious deficiencies where period expired, notify and give new time (usually 1 month) to supply omission or terminate under 37 CFR 1.550(d). Form paragraph 22.14 may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for inadvertent omissions vs deliberate omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of giving time to supply an omission applies only where the omission is inadvertent; it does not apply where there has been a deliberate omission of some necessary part of a complete response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once inadvertence is brought to the patent owner's attention, inadvertence no longer exists and a second one-month Office action to supply the same omission would not be appropriate. The practice is discretionary and should not be followed if the examiner concludes the patent owner is attempting to abuse it to obtain additional time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling responses after final Office action with omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: For bona fide responses made after a final Office action that omit necessary points, the examiner should not issue a notice of failure to fully respond; instead an advisory Office action (PTOL-467) should be issued explaining the omission. The time period in the final rejection continues to run and is extended by one month for the first response after final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after final are approved for entry only if they place the proceeding in condition for issuance of a reexamination certificate or make it in better form for appeal; otherwise they are not approved for entry. If an amendment after final does not place the proceeding in condition for issuance, prosecution continues to run until a response under 37 CFR 1.113 (notice of appeal or qualifying amendment) is filed. The examiner may, within discretion, enter the response, withdraw the final action, and issue a new action (Ex parte Quayle) where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Defective Paper (PTOL-475) — defects that can make a submission informal
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if substance is complete, a submission can be defective (informal) for reasons such as: (A) no proof of service; (B) unsigned paper; (C) signed by person not of record; (D) amendment does not comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j); (E) amendment does not comply with 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and/or (c)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PTOL-475 to notify defects; check boxes and fill blanks, and attach a separate sheet if further clarification is needed. A time period of one month (or 30 days, whichever is longer) will be set in PTOL-475 for correction. If a defective response is filed after final (but before expiration), issue PTOL-467 instead and time continues to run (extended by 1 month if first response after final).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service proof and clerk handling when service missing
rubrics_metrics.description: If no proof of service is included where required, the reexamination clerk should contact the submitting party to confirm whether service was actually made. If service is confirmed, enter the submission and annotate with 'Service confirmed by [name] on [date]'; if not, the submission is placed in the reexamination file but normally not considered and is added to the IFW file history as an unentered paper with 'N/E' notation and brief explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the party cannot be contacted, mail a Notice of Defective Paper (PTOL-475) giving one month (or 30 days, whichever is longer) to provide a supplemental paper indicating manner and date of service. Form paragraph 22.15 (Lack of Service) may be used. Failure to supply service may result in denial of consideration and, for patent owner responses, termination under 37 CFR 1.550(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to serve submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to serve a submission as required in a third-party requested reexamination may cause the submission to be refused consideration. For patent owner responses, refusal of consideration may result in termination of the reexamination proceeding under 37 CFR 1.550(d) unless the patent owner otherwise completely responded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 22.15 may be used to give notice and require certification of service within one month (or 30 days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of inappropriate or untimely papers (return, file location, Director approval)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain types of correspondence that are inappropriate or untimely will be returned or forwarded to one of three files (Reexamination File, Patent File, or Storage File). Some returns require TC Director or Director approval (e.g., premature responses by owner when owner is not requester; papers submitted on behalf of a third party).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returned papers must be accompanied by a letter indicating signature and approval of the TC Director. If a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 or 1.183 is filed with the paper, the reexamination proceeding should be forwarded to the Office of Patent Legal Administration for decision instead of immediate return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsigned papers and other defective paper types to be placed in reexamination file
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed by owner which are unsigned or signed by less than all of the owners (no attorney of record or unauthorized signer) are defective and are to be located in the reexamination file as defective papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such defective papers may be subject to PTOL-475 notification and the one-month correction period; handling should follow the defective-paper procedures described in MPEP §2266.02 and §2266.03.
